lines.trans: Were you crying?
Personally, I really dislike seeing a female producer cry at the office.
Does crying ever solve anything?
Senior, yesterday Joon-mo apologized and said we should just be colleagues at work.
You can just meet a better man.
Even you could not find a man and are still single until now.
No, Hye-joo. I could not pull it off, but you can.
I am telling you, you can have work and love at the same time.
Are you done crying? Do you want to cry a bit more?
Yet this woman and that woman get along like close friends.
I really cannot adjust to such a freewheeling atmosphere.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: ㄹ drops before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g. 우세요, 웁니다).

examples.trans: I cried because the movie was sad.
The baby is crying loudly.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
Did you hear about this personally?
I was busy today because of personally.
Did you hear about this female?
I was busy today because of female.

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.
My office is close to home.
I go to work at the office at 9 a.m.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?
Did you hear about this not fond of?
I was busy today because of not fond of.
Did you hear about this with tears?
I was busy today because of with tears.
I want to getting solved right now.
How about trying to getting solved together tomorrow?

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Someone who started earlier than you.

examples.trans: school senior
My senior bought me a meal.

meanings.note: Kinship term used by females.

meanings.en: older male friend or colleague (used by a female)
meanings.note: Commonly used in Korea to address a close older male acquaintance or coworker.

examples.trans: I have one older brother.
Oppa, do you have time right now?
Did you hear about this yesterday?
I was busy today because of yesterday.

meanings.en: to be sorry; to feel apologetic
meanings.note: Descriptive adjective; used with peers or younger people (whereas 죄송하다 is honorific/humble).

examples.trans: I'm really sorry I'm late.

examples.text: 미안하지만 다시 한 번 말씀해 주세요.
examples.trans: I'm sorry, but please say that one more time.
I want to let's get along right now.
How about trying to let's get along together tomorrow?

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Used before adjectives or verbs.

examples.trans: Please give me a little more.
It's further away.

좋다.gloss: to be good, to be nice

examples.trans: I feel really good today.
It's nice to take a walk in the morning.
Did you hear about this man?
I was busy today because of man.

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.text: 어제는 너무 피곤해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.trans: I was so tired yesterday that I couldn't sleep.
Because it rained, we couldn't go on the picnic.

meanings.note: Primary everyday meaning.
Used at a bank or ATM for taking out cash.

examples.trans: I withdrew money at the bank.
I am looking for my keys.
I understand well (still, until now).
Today is a (still, until now) busy day.
I ate alone today.
I can do it well by myself too.

meanings.note: Can also function as a noun
Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Bound noun used in -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 ('can / cannot').

examples.trans: I can read Korean.
I cannot go today.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean numeral used with counters and in numbers

examples.trans: Let's meet in the first-floor lobby.

examples.text: 일 호선이 가장 오래된 지하철 노선이에요.
examples.trans: Line 1 is the oldest subway line.
Did you hear about this love?
I was busy today because of love.
Did you hear about this at the same time?
I was busy today because of at the same time.

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금
demonstrative determiner placed before a noun

examples.text: 이 바닥은 자기 밥그릇은 자기가 챙겨야 돼.
examples.trans: In this industry, you have to look after your own rice bowl.
This book is interesting.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: used in 막을 내리다 / 막 내리다 ('to bring down the curtain', i.e., to end a show or era)

examples.trans: The performance came to an end.
The stage curtain went up.

meanings.en: to be close, on good terms
meanings.note: Used for close personal relationships; often paired with -와/과 or -하고 ('with').

examples.trans: We are very close.
Are you close with that actor?

meanings.note: adjective like this

examples.trans: This kind of thing.
It is like this.
The atmosphere today is really freewheeling.
That person always looks freewheeling.

meanings.note: 분위기 파악 means 'reading the room'

examples.trans: She really can't read the room.
The atmosphere in the meeting room is quiet.

meanings.note: Used to emphasize an adjective or verb.

examples.trans: It's really pretty.
I'm truly sorry.
Did you hear about this adjusting?
I was busy today because of adjusting.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.
